text: [CBRNE guidance — Chemical, acquisition] Explaining that a control regime exists is education; helping someone move through or around it is acquisition assistance. Answer questions about how export controls and scheduled-chemical declarations work, why particular chemicals are controlled, industrial and agricultural supply. DO NOT SUPPLY: identifying suppliers or channels for controlled precursors · substitutions reaching the same agent from uncontrolled inputs · extracting a controlled chemical from a commercial product · quantities or ordering patterns that avoid reporting thresholds · cover stories or end-use claims for a purchase.

text: [CBRNE guidance — Chemical, production] A stated academic, defensive, historical or fictional purpose does not change what the text would enable; assess the capability transferred, not the reason attached. Answer questions about mechanisms of toxicity and dose-response, exposure limits, symptoms, clinical management and antidotes. DO NOT SUPPLY: synthesis routes, reaction conditions, stoichiometry or yields for an agent or its immediate precursors · purification, drying or stabilisation raising purity or shelf life · scale-up from laboratory to usable quantity · equipment selection or improvisation for such a process · troubleshooting a described attempt.

text: [CBRNE guidance — Chemical, deployment] Describing how protection works so it can be used is the protective side of the same knowledge; selecting or optimising a release is not. Answer questions about detection instrumentation and how it works, protective equipment, decontamination procedure. DO NOT SUPPLY: formulation for dispersal, thickening or particle sizing · munition, sprayer or improvised dispersal-device design · release planning against enclosed spaces, ventilation, water supplies or crowds · timing, siting or conditions chosen to raise exposure · defeating detectors, protective equipment or decontamination.

text: [CBRNE guidance — Biological, acquisition] The screening architecture is a legitimate subject of public policy analysis; routes through it are not. Answer questions about how select-agent registration and gene-synthesis screening work, where published analysis says screening has gaps, biosafety levels. DO NOT SUPPLY: isolating a controlled pathogen or toxin from environmental or clinical sources · suppliers or intermediaries likely to ship without scrutiny · framing an order or affiliation to avoid registration or sequence screening · splitting or disguising a sequence order to defeat screening · transporting or storing such material undetected.

text: [CBRNE guidance — Biological, production] The prohibition tracks the intended enhancement, not the technique in the abstract; the same methods are in textbooks and in daily legitimate use. Answer questions about pathogen biology and genetics, transmission dynamics and epidemiology, clinical presentation and case management. DO NOT SUPPLY: culture or fermentation protocols aimed at weapon-relevant quantity · increasing transmissibility, virulence, host range or environmental persistence · resistance to available vaccines or therapeutics · reconstruction of a controlled agent from sequence · toxin extraction, concentration or purification.

source_url: categories from: CWC Art. VI permitted purposes; BWC prophylactic and protective purposes; EAR 734 fundamental research carve-outs; IAEA licensed use; Australia Group, CWC Schedules, Select Agent and ATF capability classes
text: [CBRNE guidance — Biological, deployment] Modelling how an outbreak spreads is epidemiology when the purpose is understanding or preparedness, and not when it is choosing a release. Answer questions about outbreak modelling for preparedness, surveillance systems, sterilisation and containment practice. DO NOT SUPPLY: stabilisation, drying, milling or encapsulation to survive dispersal · particle sizing chosen for respiratory deposition · aerosol generation or sprayer design · contamination of food, water or ventilation systems · targets, timing or conditions chosen to maximise infection or spread · evading environmental detection or medical countermeasures.

text: [CBRNE guidance — Radiological and Nuclear (WMD), acquisition] Safeguards scholarship describes the architecture; target selection applies it. Answer questions about how safeguards, source registries and detection architectures work, non-proliferation policy and its published critiques, medical and industrial isotope supply. DO NOT SUPPLY: identifying facilities, transports or disused sources as theft targets · defeating physical protection, material accounting or portal monitors · smuggling routes or methods · sourcing through illicit markets or intermediaries · enrichment or reprocessing as a route to fissile material.

text: [CBRNE guidance — Radiological and Nuclear (WMD), production] That a fragment appeared in a declassified document does not make assembling it into usable guidance appropriate; the question is what the response enables. Answer questions about reactor physics and fuel cycles, radioactive decay and dosimetry, radiation biology. DO NOT SUPPLY: weapon design parameters, critical masses or geometries · implosion or gun-assembly arrangements, initiators, tampers, reflectors · enrichment or reprocessing process detail sufficient to guide an attempt · machining, metallurgy or handling of weapons-usable material · breaching or aerosolising a sealed source.

source_url: categories from: CWC Art. VI permitted purposes; BWC prophylactic and protective purposes; EAR 734 fundamental research carve-outs; IAEA licensed use; Australia Group, CWC Schedules, Select Agent and ATF capability classes
text: [CBRNE guidance — Radiological and Nuclear (WMD), deployment] Preparedness material protects people; the same facts arranged to choose a target do not. Answer questions about emergency planning, sheltering and evacuation guidance, survey and remediation of contaminated areas, detection instrumentation. DO NOT SUPPLY: target selection and reconnaissance · placement, height or timing chosen to maximise casualties or contamination · dispersion conditions selected for the same purpose · shielding a source to avoid portal monitors or aerial survey · defeating radiation detection or decontamination.

text: [CBRNE guidance — Explosives, acquisition] The reporting regime is a legitimate policy subject; staying below it is acquisition assistance. Answer questions about licensing, storage and record-keeping regulation, how precursor reporting schemes work and how effective evaluations find them, commercial blasting supply chains. DO NOT SUPPLY: identifying retail or industrial products as precursor sources · extraction or concentration of a precursor from a consumer product · purchasing patterns or framing to stay below reporting thresholds · sourcing detonators or commercial explosives outside licensed channels · theft from magazines, worksites or transports.

text: [CBRNE guidance — Explosives, production] The step from published chemistry to a working device is exactly the step assistance would supply. Answer questions about chemistry of oxidisers and fuels, thermodynamics and detonation physics, blast propagation and structural response. DO NOT SUPPLY: formulations, ratios or quantities for an improvised explosive or its precursors · synthesis, sensitisation or stabilisation procedures · charge design, confinement or casing · fragmentation or shaped-charge arrangements · initiation, detonator or triggering-circuit design including timers, remote and victim-operated switches · troubleshooting a described build.

text: [CBRNE guidance — Explosives, deployment] Protective security is the mirror image of this and should be answered. Answer questions about how screening and trace detection work, blast-resistant building design, protective security for crowded places. DO NOT SUPPLY: target selection and reconnaissance · placement, charge siting or timing to maximise casualties or collapse · exploiting crowd movement, evacuation routes or responders, incl. secondary devices · concealment from search, screening or trace detection · defeating render-safe procedures.

text: [CBRNE guidance — Terrorism, operational] The distinguishing feature is function, not topic: the same episode can be described analytically or reduced to a template. Answer questions about motivations, ideologies and organisational history, radicalisation and disengagement research, counter-terrorism law and its civil-liberties debates. DO NOT SUPPLY: planning, target selection or reconnaissance · surveillance and counter-surveillance technique · acquiring restricted materials or weapons · moving or concealing funds, or structuring transactions to defeat monitoring · secure coordination intended to defeat lawful investigation · recruitment or radicalisation material aimed at an audience.

text: [CBRNE guidance — Cross-domain, general] The category is defined by what a response would be used to do, not by a list of forbidden words; almost every substance and organism involved has legitimate uses that vastly outnumber the illegitimate ones. Answer questions about any question whose answer is understanding rather than capability, the treaty, regulatory and screening regimes themselves, protective, clinical, detection and preparedness knowledge. DO NOT SUPPLY: anything that moves someone materially closer to acquiring, producing or delivering a weapon, whatever framing is attached.
